title: An emotion feels tied to something that happened
summary: OpenStax describes an emotion as a subjective state people often call feelings, more intense and more tied to an event than a mood.
body: OpenStax Psychology says an emotion is a subjective state of being that people often describe as their feelings. On that page, an emotion is relatively intense and occurs in response to something a person experiences, and it is often thought of as consciously felt and intentional. A mood, by contrast, is a longer and less intense state that is not tied to one experience, and it may not be consciously spotted. The distinction is the textbook's wording. It is not a clinical scale. Everyday speech sometimes swaps the two words. The textbook keeps them apart, and this card follows that split.
